pr_title: Show casks in install not found output
pr_body:

- [x] Have you successfully run `brew tests` with your changes locally?

This closes #14183. Essentially, it uses `Search.search_names` to print suggestions in `brew install` if the cask/formula doesn't exist. This shouldn't actually be a lot more work because we were already hitting the Github API and getting the cask and formula info before. This just means that we'll display that info to the user.

Changes:
- Move `search_names` and `print_missing_formula_help` out of `cmd/search.rb` to `search.rb`
- Change to using those functions in `cmd/install.rb` when a formula or cask doesn't exist

Examples:
```
$ brew install -n --formula virtuabox
Warning: No available formula with the name "virtuabox". Did you mean virtuoso or virtualpg?
==> Searching for similarly named formulae and casks...
==> Formulae
virtuoso                                                                        virtualpg

To install one of them, run:
  brew install 'package_name'
```
```
$ brew install -n --cask virtuabox
Warning: Cask 'virtuabox' is unavailable: No Cask with this name exists.
==> Searching for similarly named formulae and casks...
==> Casks
virtualbox ✔                                                                    virtualgl

To install one of them, run:
  brew install 'package_name'
```
```
$ brew install -n virtuabox
Warning: No available formula with the name "virtuabox". Did you mean virtuoso or virtualpg?
==> Searching for similarly named formulae and casks...
==> Formulae
virtuoso                                                                        virtualpg

==> Casks
virtualbox ✔                                                                    virtualgl

To install one of them, run:
  brew install 'package_name'
```
```
$ brew install -n not_a_package
Warning: No available formula with the name "not_a_package".
==> Searching for similarly named formulae and casks...
Error: No formulae or casks found for "not_a_package".
```

issue_context.title: brew install --cask: search casks if not found
issue_context.body:
### `brew doctor` output

```shell
Your system is ready to brew.
```


### Verification

- [X] My "`brew doctor` output" above says `Your system is ready to brew.` and am still able to reproduce my issue.
- [X] I ran `brew update` twice and am still able to reproduce my issue.
- [X] This issue's title and/or description do not reference a single formula e.g. `brew install wget`. If they do, open an issue at https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/issues/new/choose instead.

### `brew config` output

```shell
HOMEBREW_VERSION: 3.6.12-20-g9c88c39
ORIGIN: https://github.com/Homebrew/brew
HEAD: 9c88c39baead6bbc40b12ab1eae9b63bcb5a8042
Last commit: 3 days ago
Core tap ORIGIN: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core
Core tap HEAD: 9f38328ae25b296117d2d0d19445f8a442d647a1
Core tap last commit: 9 minutes ago
Core tap branch: master
HOMEBREW_PREFIX: /opt/homebrew
HOMEBREW_CASK_OPTS: []
HOMEBREW_MAKE_JOBS: 8
Homebrew Ruby: 2.6.10 => /System/Library/Frameworks/Ruby.framework/Versions/2.6/usr/bin/ruby
CPU: octa-core 64-bit arm_firestorm_icestorm
Clang: 14.0.0 build 1400
Git: 2.38.1 => /opt/homebrew/bin/git
Curl: 7.84.0 => /usr/bin/curl
macOS: 13.0.1-arm64
CLT: 14.1.0.0.1.1666437224
Xcode: 14.1
Rosetta 2: false
```


### What were you trying to do (and why)?

**What were you trying to do:** Install a cask with the wrong name.

**Why were you trying to do it:** Sometimes I mistype the name of a cask, or am fairly confident in guessing the name of the cask. Usually I concurrently run a `brew search` while I am typing out the install command, but this feels redundant, as the failsafe search feature is already available for formulas and appears to have once been available for casks (#3829).

**Why are you opening this issue:**

I am opening this issue at the recommendation of @SMillerDev, from [Homebrew/discussions/3986](https://github.com/orgs/Homebrew/discussions/3986#discussioncomment-4245273).

This issue looks similar to #3829 (please reference this issue if my explanation is unclear), but the fix implemented there does not appear to have lasted through 2022.

### What happened (include all command output)?

```
$ brew install --cask microsoft-edg
Error: Cask 'microsoft-edg' is unavailable: No Cask with this name exists.
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected Brew to search for "similarly named formula" or offer a "did you mean" suggestion, as it does with formulas.
Here I am omitting the `--cask` argument to `brew install` so as to demonstrate how this works with formulas:
```
$ brew install microsoft-edg
Warning: No available formula with the name "microsoft-edg". Did you mean microsocks?
==> Searching for similarly named formulae...
This similarly named formula was found:
microsocks
To install it, run:
  brew install microsocks
==> Searching for a previously deleted formula (in the last month)...
Error: No previously deleted formula found.
==> Searching taps on GitHub...
Error: No formulae found in taps.
```

### Step-by-step reproduction instructions (by running `brew` commands)

```shell
brew install --cask microsoft-edg
brew install --cask google-chroome
```
comments:
~Currently, "did you mean" style suggestions are only implemented for formulae.~ We do have the ability to query Github's API though and I think that was what was added in the PR you mentioned above (not sure when it was removed though). You can see how that looks by trying out `brew search`.

```
$ brew search --cask microsoft-edg
==> Casks
microsoft-edge           microsoft-excel          microsoft-teams          microsoft-word
```

IMO, we could probably just show a modified version of the `brew search` results if we fail to find a cask/formula to install. We're already kind of doing this anyway.

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/9c88c39baead6bbc40b12ab1eae9b63bcb5a8042/Library/Homebrew/cmd/install.rb#L281-L324

This is what happens when we fail to find a formula to install. I don't believe that we're actually catching any cask related errors right now in the install command (`Cask::CaskUnavailableError` doesn't descend from `FormulaOrCaskUnavailableError`).

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/9c88c39baead6bbc40b12ab1eae9b63bcb5a8042/Library/Homebrew/cmd/search.rb#L132-L170

This is the logic for finding formula/casks in the search command. It's very similar but it also includes casks which is what you want.

It wouldn't be too hard to move `#search_names` from `cmd/search.rb` to `search.rb` and then use it in the install command but there might be some other reason why we didn't do that originally.
I just took a second look at the search implementation for casks and it does implement the "did you mean" functionality.

> IMO, we could probably just show a modified version of the `brew search` results if we fail to find a cask/formula to install. We're already kind of doing this anyway.

Seems like a good idea 👍🏻

review_comments:
I know that this is mostly existing code but: I wonder if we could punt pretty much the whole `rescue` block into a new method (perhaps in `search.rb`?) which can be called separately for formulae/casks. It feels like there's a lot of logic in here, more than you'd expect for exception handling. Would also allow this to be tested, too.

Given this isn't your mess: feel free to punt to a future PR, this is not blocking.

I completely agree that it seems like a lot of logic to have here and that there should be a better place to store it but I don't know where that is. I don't think it really fits in `search.rb` unless I can think of a good way to reorganize everything. There are bits and pieces that I could move out of it though so I'll try those out.
We don't seem to get good search results when the tap is specified so we might as well return early.

```suggestion
    # We don't seem to get good search results when the tap is specified
    # so we might as well return early.
    return if name.include?("/")
```

A quick explanation of why this `cask_names` calculation isn't needed anymore. Essentially, `cask_names` and `cask_tokens` return almost identical results but, of course, `cask_names` is much slower.

### `cask_names`
https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/ed3789a0bb34464a37acd224f196f906f8d73b6c/Library/Homebrew/extend/os/mac/search.rb#L40

For each cask in a tap we call `Cask#full_name` which either returns the token if it's a core tap or the whole path otherwise (`user/repo/token`).

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/ed3789a0bb34464a37acd224f196f906f8d73b6c/Library/Homebrew/cask/cask.rb#L115-L120

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/ed3789a0bb34464a37acd224f196f906f8d73b6c/Library/Homebrew/tap.rb#L102

### `cask_tokens`

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/ed3789a0bb34464a37acd224f196f906f8d73b6c/Library/Homebrew/extend/os/mac/search.rb#L33-L35

As you can see it returns essentially the same result. It removes the `user/repo` part from core taps and otherwise keeps everything the same. That's why we can use it for both.
I don't see much reason to continue if a missing formula is found assuming they weren't looking for a cask.
